pillarForecast.why: Pursuers trail behind him while rocks stream left into them, so many rock kills happen without a deliberate setup. He'll enjoy watching them smash at first, but he may again feel the kills are more accidental than planned.
Danger now comes from the situation in front of him (density, speed), which he can see, and sectors escalate visibly. B's speed reads as intensity.
Sector 1 is deliberately sparse and A cruises at 95 px/s. That echoes run 3's 'slow to start', especially on repeat runs from sector 1.
Pursuers enter from the left edge, just behind a player who starts at x=0.3 looking right at the field. A hit from behind that he never saw could feel cheap.
Progress is visible (bar), but the pace is fixed at 40s per sector. He liked setting the pace himself, so he may ask for a way to influence speed.
A full flight is 4 minutes, which answers 'we might need more levels'. A residual risk is that it feels long once it's learned.
He has accepted 2 hearts and dangerous rocks quietly. A strong player with a heart back per sector should get deep quickly.

biggestRisk: The flight is a fixed 4-minute conveyor: the scroll, not the player, sets the pace, and every sector lasts exactly 40s. Once the novelty of his own idea wears off (by runs 19-20), and especially in the slower variant A, it may feel like being carried through rather than choosing a route. Kills come mostly from rocks running into pursuers behind him rather than traps he set. Expect 'slow', 'samey' or a request for speed control or variation, not a complaint about difficulty.
abVerdict: Speed is visible, so unlike v4 he will probably notice (~70%). Leaning B (fast), ~55%, likely expressed as 'faster felt more intense/better' on run 18 or as 'slower again' on run 19. About 20% he prefers A for the room to set traps, and about 25% he doesn't name a preference or answers with a third option (letting him control the speed, e.g. pushing right to go faster).
